jobs.title: Corporate Lending Asia, SVP/VP
jobs.descriptionText:
About the Role
BBVA is seeking an experienced corporate loan professional to support the growth of its Corporate Lending franchise in China. Based in Shanghai, the successful candidate will play a pivotal role in accelerating the origination, structuring, and execution of corporate lending transactions across Mainland China.
Position level (VP or SVP) will be determined based on the selected candidate’s depth of experience and interview assessment.
Key Responsibilities
Originate corporate lending opportunities across Mainland China, including syndicated, club, bilateral, sustainable, and event-driven financings.
Structure bespoke financing solutions tailored to clients’ strategic objectives, capital structures, and risk profiles.
Prepare high-quality pitch books, proposals, and marketing materials to secure mandates and convert opportunities into executed transactions.
Negotiate commercial terms, covenants, and security packages with clients.
Draft, review, and finalize loan documentation and syndication materials, including term sheets, mandate letters, facility agreements, information memoranda, bank meeting presentations and financial models.
Prepare and present comprehensive transaction proposals to business and credit committees, clearly articulating deal structures, key risks, and lending considerations.
Take ownership of day-to-day transaction execution, coordinating closely with internal teams (Client Coverage, Loan Syndicate & Sales, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Tax, Sustainable Finance, Markets, and Operations) and external stakeholders (clients, partner banks, and legal counsel) to ensure seamless delivery.
Work with senior team members and coach junior team members, fostering high-performance deal execution capabilities and a collaborative team environment.
Qualification & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics or a related discipline
Minimum of 8+ years of corporate loan origination, structuring and execution experience
Knowledge & Skills
Track Record: Proven history of originating, negotiating and executing complex syndicated and bilateral loan mandates in the Chinese market.
Technical Expertise: Advanced credit analysis, debt structuring, financial modeling and loan documentation skills.
Regulatory & Market Knowledge: Sound understanding of China’s corporate debt market (both onshore and offshore), and relevant regulatory frameworks.
Soft Skills: Collaborative team player with outstanding interpersonal and presentation abilities; highly organized, detail-oriented, and capable of managing multi-stream transactions under tight timeframes.
Language
Native or professional fluency in both Mandarin and English (written and spoken) is required

jobs.title: Compliance Manager, Shanghai Branch
jobs.descriptionText:
Job Purpose & Objectives
Assist and support business management in identifying, assessing, measuring and mitigating compliance risks.
Provide reasonable assurance that the Bank and its employees comply with applicable laws, regulations, internal rules and ethical standards within the context of corporate governance.
Handle regulatory issues related to business partners and ensure appropriate management escalation.
Manage relationships and develop mutual understanding with the regulators and monitoring authorities with respect to compliance matters.
Work closely with business partners to broaden and deepen their knowledge and behaviour on business and industry specific regulatory requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Provide advice and support to the business units and management with regard to potential regulatory impacts of relevant laws, rules, regulations and guidelines.
Participate in reviewing new business/new product initiatives and provide compliance input to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and internal policies.
Provide advice on KYC documentation and transactions screening, and monitor transaction alerts to ensure compliance with relevant anti-money laundering and sanction regulations.
Provide compliance advice on GM business operations and activities surveillance.
Prepare and update policies and procedures in line with Group Policy and with regard to local laws, rules, regulations and guidelines.
Conduct compliance induction to new joiners and provide training to relevant staff on changes and development of laws, rules, regulations and guidelines.
Ensure business activities are properly licensed and all relevant staff are properly registered with regulators as appropriate.
Monitor key compliance issues and ensure prompt escalation to senior management or designated committee.
Liaise with relevant regulators for any regulatory enquiries and compliance related issues.
Assist in regulatory reviews conducted by regulators and help prepare regulatory reporting, filings and self-assessments as required.
Perform compliance review on business units in accordance with the standards and guidelines contained in the compliance monitoring plan.
Assist in any other ad hoc projects.
Qualification & Experience
Degree holder in Finance, Accounting or Laws
At least 8 years compliance experience in financial institutions
Knowledge & Skills
In-depth knowledge of regulatory and compliance requirements in relation to banking business especially in Sustainability & Financial Market, AML&CTF and Data Protection.
Well-versed with banking services and financial products
PC literacy (Microsoft Office including word, excel and powerpoint)
Language
Proficient in written and spoken English
Proficient in written and spoken Chinese
Other Skills (e.g. Interpersonal, Communication etc)
Strong interpersonal and communication skills
Customer-oriented
Well-organized and meticulous in details
Ability to work in a matrix reporting structure, multi-functional and cross-cultural environment
Ability to work independently, self-motivated and be a team player
Ability to work under pressure

jobs.title: Corporate Lending Asia, Analyst / Associate, Shanghai/HK Based
jobs.descriptionText:
Description
BBVA’s Corporate Lending Asia team is seeking a motivated corporate banking professional to support the origination, structuring, and execution of corporate loan transactions across the Asia-Pacific region. Based in Hong Kong or Shanghai, this role is embedded within the regional platform and plays an integral part in delivering live deals across the full transaction lifecycle.
Working closely with senior originators and key stakeholders, the successful candidate will cover syndicated loans,acquisition financings, sustainable finance, and bespoke credit solutions. Primary market coverage is China, with scope to expand regionally over time.
This position offers deep exposure to complex credit transactions and progressive career growth within a dynamic, expanding business.
Key Responsibilities:
▪ Support corporate lending transactions across all stages of the deal lifecycle, including credit analysis, pitch preparation, term sheet development, loan structuring, and documentation, contributing to high-quality deal delivery
▪ Conduct market, industry, and company research to generate insights that support credit, pricing, and structuring decisions
▪ Maintain and analyze precedent and comparable transaction data to support market intelligence, deal origination and strategic decisions
▪ Prepare and present proposals to business and credit committees for deal approvals
▪ Draft, review, and coordinate loan and syndication documentation, including term sheets, mandate letters, facility agreements, fee letters, and information memoranda
▪ Collaborate closely with internal teams – including Coverage, Risk, Loan Syndicate and Sales, Legal, Compliance, Tax, Sustainable Finance, Operations – as well as external stakeholders such as clients, partner banks and legal counsel to ensure smooth and timely transaction execution
▪ Manage transaction closings, including documentation execution, internal loan booking, and the
preparation of internal and external case studies and post-deal analyses
▪ Prepare management presentations and pipeline activity reports
▪ Ensure compliance with internal policies, audit standards, filing requirements, and documentation
procedures for all completed transactions
Qualifications
▪ Bachelor degree in Finance, Economics or a related discipline
▪ Minimum 2-4 years of relevant experience in corporate loan origination, debt structuring, or loan
syndication within corporate or investment banking.
Knowledge & Skills
▪ Demonstrated experience in corporate loan origination, debt structuring, and end-to-end deal
execution.
▪ Strong corporate credit analysis, financial modeling, debt capacity assessment, and risk management
capabilities.
▪ Highly organized self-starter capable of managing multiple live deal tracks under tight deadlines with high precision.
▪ Excellent analytical, presentation, and stakeholder management skills with a strong client focus.
▪ Proficient in MS Office, Bloomberg, and Refinitiv (LoanConnector)
Language
▪ Fluent in spoken and written English and Mandarin

jobs.descriptionText:
The Global Client Executive is a pivotal, senior-level role responsible for managing and growing our most important top-tier corporate client relationships. You will serve as the primary interface for a dedicated client portfolio, acting as their advocate within Citi and a trusted strategic advisor. Your mission is to drive revenue growth and retention by ensuring an unparalleled client experience, fostering deep partnerships with key decision-makers, and strategically aligning Citi’s products and services with their business objectives.
Detailed Responsibilities
Client Relationship Management:
Cultivate and maintain strong, long-lasting partnerships with key client executives and decision-makers, establishing yourself as a trusted advisor for their treasury and financial needs.
Strategic Revenue Growth:
Take commercial ownership of your client portfolio. Identify and pursue opportunities for strategic growth, including cross-selling and up-selling of Treasury and Trade Solutions, to meet and exceed revenue targets.
Data-Driven Strategic Insight:
Leverage client feedback, performance data, and market trend analysis to provide strategic insights that enhance client satisfaction, inform investment decisions, and foster measurable business growth.
Executive-Level Client Advocacy:
Champion client needs within the organization. Collaborate seamlessly with internal partners across Sales, Product, Operations, and Service to resolve complex issues promptly and ensure superior client outcomes.
Strategic Account Planning:
Lead proactive relationship reviews with key clients to understand their strategic objectives. Develop and execute comprehensive account plans that drive product adoption, ensure revenue realization, and align with the client’s long-term goals.
Proactive Stakeholder Communication:
Ensure internal stakeholders are proactively informed of client needs, product requirements, and strategic priorities to foster alignment and drive execution.
Development Value
This role offers significant strategic development opportunities, including:
In-depth Strategic Understanding:
Cultivate a profound understanding of customer Treasury organizations, specific industries, treasury functions, and the Treasury and Trade Services (TTS) business, its products, risks, and controls, enhancing strategic insight.
Expanded Global Network & Strategic Relationships:
Grow your Citi network across the globe, establishing key strategic relationships that drive business outcomes.
Accelerated Career Advancement:
Expand and strengthen strategic knowledge, paving the way for advanced opportunities within Sales, Product, or Risk leadership
Qualifications
A university degree or Equivalent experience.
5+ years of work experience in a senior client-facing role within corporate banking, relationship management, or sales, with a proven track record of leading high-impact strategic projects.
Strategic Thinking:
Ability to develop forward-looking plans that deliver sustainable growth and a competitive advantage.
Leadership:
Proven experience in motivating and guiding cross-functional teams to achieve ambitious strategic goals.
Business Acumen:
A deep understanding of global business, financial drivers, and the treasury solutions landscape.
Communication & Influence:
Exceptional verbal and written skills with the ability to influence, negotiate, and strategically engage diverse internal and external stakeholders at a senior level.
Problem-Solving:
A strong analytical mindset with the ability to identify complex challenges and design innovative, strategic solutions.
A proven track record of autonomous strategic leadership, ownership, and independent execution of complex tasks.
Diversity & Inclusion
Citi values diversity. We appreciate a diverse workforce and recognize that differences in style and perspective add strategic value to decisions, actions, and organizational success.
Citi is an Equal Opportunities Employer.
Working Environment: office setting, minimal travel required.
Effort: minimal physical effort required.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of
Senior Business Analyst
.
Business: CTO Data Technology
Job ID: 60580
Principal Responsibilities
Lead requirement scoping, business analysis, and functional design for transforming legacy core banking and customer data systems into modernized target platforms.s
Analyze online transactions, screen workflows, and batch processes to define common user journeys, functional specifications, and detailed user stories with technical acceptance criteria.
Act as the primary bridge between Business Operations, Product Owners, and IT delivery teams (API, backend, and testing) to ensure solutions align with operational needs and technical feasibility.
Drive end-to-end delivery across the project lifecycle, including requirement sign-off, screen-to-screen mapping, show-and-tell demos, UAT planning, live proofing (PVT), and rollout support.
Embed operational risk controls, data governance policies, and regulatory audit standards (e.g. dual control, segregation of duties, access management, and statutory record retention) into system requirements.
Manage backlog prioritization, resolve screen and system dependencies, and escalate delivery risks and blockers to project leadership and governance committees.
Support legacy system decommissioning by analyzing legacy data structures, screen dependencies, and operational workarounds to ensure seamless migration to target platforms.
Provide post-implementation support, incident analysis, and continuous process enhancements during BAU transition.
Requirements
Functional knowledge
Strong domain knowledge of Hong Kong banking operations, customer data (CUS), and core banking systems across retail and wholesale business lines (WPB and CMB/WSB).
In-depth understanding of banking products and servicing processes, including deposits, account maintenance, transactions, payments, and digital banking channels (BIB/PIB).
Practical understanding of KYC, customer onboarding, and account lifecycle servicing operations.
Solid grasp of banking risk governance, operational risk controls (including Maker-Checker / dual authorization, tiered approvals), and internal/external audit remediation (MSII closure).
Working knowledge of banking regulatory standards, data privacy, audit logging, and statutory data retention requirements (e.g. 7-year online record maintenance).
Technical skills
Proven track record of working in Agile, Scrum, and Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) environments, driving sprint planning and regular release cycles.
Practical experience in legacy system migration, including screen-to-screen mapping, legacy demise, batch-to-online transition, and system interface analysis.
Understanding of modern enterprise application architecture, including Microservices, Process APIs (PAPI), frontend/UI frameworks, and backend data integration.
Proficiency in project and requirement management tools, particularly Jira and Confluence.
Strong technical problem-solving capabilities to define system pre-check validation rules, automated checks, and error-handling workflows to mitigate manual operational risk.
Familiarity with CI/CD delivery pipelines, deployment verification, and defect triage management.
Communication and soft skills
Proven stakeholder management capability, with the ability to build trust and align priorities across Business Operations, IT engineering, Architecture, and Risk Stewards.
Strong negotiation and problem-solving skills to balance operational demands against technical constraints under tight regulatory and delivery milestones.
Demonstrated experience facilitating cross-functional workshops, show-and-tell demonstrations, and requirement walk-throughs for working-level and senior management audiences.
High adaptability and resilience in managing multiple priorities within complex, matrixed regional and global team structures.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English; fluency in Cantonese and/or Mandarin is an advantage.
Others
University degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
Minimum 5 years of business analysis or project delivery experience within banking IT, with proven involvement in core banking platforms, customer systems, or large-scale migration programmes.
Professional certifications in Agile or Project Management (such as SAFe PO/PM, SAFe Scrum Master, PMI-ACP, or PMP) are highly preferred.
Prior experience collaborating with global shared services (GSC) and offshore delivery centres across different geographic locations.

Business:CTO
Principal Responsibilities
Backend architecture & delivery for RAG (incl. Graph RAG & agentic search): Design and implement core RAG backend capabilities, including retrieval, re-ranking, context construction, prompt orchestration, response aggregation, Graph RAG patterns (entity/relation extraction, graph traversal, graph-grounded context assembly), and agentic search (multi-step query planning, iterative retrieval, tool/function calling).
Build pipelines for multi-modal and multi-type data (documents, emails, wikis, images, tables, logs, structured sources), including extraction/OCR, chunking, enrichment, embedding, and incremental re-indexing with rollback.
Retrieval, ranking & graph reasoning optimisation: Implement hybrid retrieval (BM25/vector/structured filters), multi-stage recall, reranking (cross-encoder/LLM), deduplication/diversity controls, and graph-based retrieval strategies to improve relevance, explainability, and traceability.
Grounded, supported answer generation: Build generation workflows that produce grounded answers with explicit support (citations, quoted evidence snippets, and source metadata), including answer structuring, confidence/scoring signals, refusal/insufficient-evidence handling, and traceable “why this answer” outputs for auditability.
Security & compliance: Implement access controls (RBAC/ABAC), data classification and masking, audit logging, encryption, and secrets management; ensure retrieval and generation flows meet bank-grade compliance requirements.
Data governance & lineage: Enforce data ownership, classification, retention, and access policies; maintain metadata standards, lineage, and provenance (citations/attribution) to ensure outputs are grounded in approved sources.
Quality evaluation & continuous improvement: Establish offline/online evaluation (groundedness, faithfulness, citation coverage, latency), enabling A/B testing and regression validation.
Cross-team collaboration: Partner with AI Infra, data platforms, information security, and product teams to land RAG capabilities in multiple systems and continuously evolve the platform.
Requirements
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
5+ years of backend engineering experience; strong proficiency in at least one mainstream backend stack: Python (FastAPI) or Go.
Solid understanding of core RAG components and patterns, including chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, context window management, citations/attribution, and evaluation.
Hands-on experience with containerisation and cloud-native engineering (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD), with a proven track record of troubleshooting and performance tuning in production.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to deliver under multi-dimensional constraints (security, compliance, performance, and cost).
Demonstrates an AI-native mindset, applying AI-driven approaches to improve productivity, quality, and decision-making.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Morgan Stanley Investment Management China (MSIM China), strives to provide diverse investment management services to a full spectrum of clients across both individual and institutional investors. Established as a joint venture in 2008, MSIM China became fully owned by Morgan Stanley Investment Management in 2023.

Benefiting from the global perspective and risk management capability of Morgan Stanley, MSIM China has established a variety of mutual fund and private fund portfolios covering fixed income, active equity, quantitative equity, multi-asset and sustainable investing strategies. Our portfolios have won many prestigious awards, including Morningstar Awards and Golden Bull Awards, which is a testament to our expertise and capabilities.

What You'll Do

Primary responsibilities will include advising investment professionals and directing outside counsel in connection with investment activities and fund structuring as well as compliance requirements arising from various regulatory and internal policy obligations.

The candidate will be responsible for legal coverage within MSIM China’s business including:

  • Interacting regularly with senior management in the business, Risk Officers, Compliance, Tax, Finance and other stakeholders to manage legal risk and protect the Firm’s reputation;
  • Providing coverage for legal aspects of fund structuring, fund formation and fund governance for complex fund structures;
  • Instructing external counsels;
  • Advising on changes in law, new regulatory initiatives and changing market practices for funds and related investments;
  • Advising on the development and execution of internal policies and procedures;
  • Drafting and reviewing legal documents related to MSIM China’s products (mutual products and private offered products) to ensure the products are legal and compliant;
  • Responsible for reviewing various Chinese and English contracts or legal documents related to MSIM China’s operations, and providing legal advice on any issues encountered during contract performance;
  • Track changes in laws and regulations, regulatory requirements and industry rules, conduct legal researches, and participate in the implementation of new regulations;
  • Propose revision suggestions on MSIM China’s Articles of Association and internal policies, and participate in corporate governance;
  • Assist in dealing with disputes, litigation and arbitration involving companies and products as needed, and coordinate with external lawyers to safeguard the company's rights and interests;
  • Cooperate with other business departments in legal work;
  • Working closely with regional colleagues;
  • Other affairs arranged by the manager.

What You’ll Bring

  • Master degree in Law from key domestic or international universities (Undergraduate degree in Law is preferred).
  • Lawyer with 5+ years relevant post-qualification experience preferably in financial institutions, such as fund management companies, asset management companies, or first-class law firms serving financial clients.
  • Must have passed the National Judicial Examination (Qualified for the Legal Professional Qualification Certificate A), Fund Practitioner Qualification Certificate and Lawyer Qualification Certificate are preferred.
  • Familiar with laws and regulations in fund industry, familiar with legal theories and practices in the fields of company law, contract law, security law, property law, trust law, etc.;
  • Solid drafting and negotiation skills.
  • A personable and confident disposition, with the ability to identify and resolve disputes in a fast-paced corporate environment while adhering to Firm policies and practices.
  • Proficient in English, listening, speaking, reading and writing. Capable of independently drafting and reviewing English contracts and proficient in English conversations with regional/ global colleagues.
  • Team player with solid analytical and presentation skills.

What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work. To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.

Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences.

For more information, please visit: https://www.morganstanley.com/people-opportunities/eeo

jobs.title: MSIM China, Financial Crime Risk (1st Line), VP/SA, Shenzhen
jobs.descriptionText:
Company Overview
Morgan Stanley Investment Management China (MSIM China), strives to provide diverse investment management services to a full spectrum of clients across both individual and institutional investors. Established as a joint venture in 2008, MSIM China became fully owned by Morgan Stanley Investment Management in 2023.
Benefiting from the global perspective and risk management capability of Morgan Stanley, MSIM China has established a variety of mutual fund and private fund portfolios covering fixed income, active equity, quantitative equity, multi-asset and sustainable investing strategies. Our portfolios have won many prestigious awards, including Morningstar Awards and Golden Bull Awards, which is a testament to our expertise and capabilities.
Position Overview
The first-line Financial Crimes Risk team is embedded within the Investment Management business and serves as the first line of defense for financial-crimes risk. It is responsible for identifying, assessing, escalating and helping to remediate money-laundering, sanctions and reputational risks associated with the firm’s funds, managed accounts, distribution partners and clients. The team owns first-line know-your-customer (KYC), enhanced due diligence, screening and onboarding oversight, working within the firm’s global financial-crimes framework and in close partnership with the regional and global Financial Crimes functions, the business, Operations, Technology and Legal & Compliance. This role delivers dedicated onshore coverage for the Investment Management business in China while operating under the direction of the regional Financial Crimes function.
The Vice President, Financial Crimes Risk, is the dedicated onshore first-line financial-crimes resource for the firm’s Investment Management business in China, based in Shenzhen. Reporting to the local Chief Operating Office and matrixed into the regional Financial Crimes Risk team, the role provides advisory support and risk oversight across customer onboarding, screening, enhanced due diligence, transaction reviews and financial-crimes initiatives.
Working closely with Operations, Compliance, Legal and the business, and taking direction from the regional and global Financial Crimes functions, the role helps drive effective risk management, regulatory compliance and operational excellence as local anti-money-laundering (AML) and KYC requirements continue to expand – including full-population periodic reviews, enhanced screening, and multi-year AML systems transformation. A dedicated onshore presence is essential to engage local stakeholders in real time, meet local data-residency and privacy requirements, and ensure consistent, well-coordinated execution between the onshore business and the wider Financial Crimes organization.
What you'll do in the role: (1LOD)
Serve as the dedicated onshore first-line point of contact and financial-crimes subject-matter expert for the Investment Management business in China, providing real-time advisory and escalation support to Operations, Compliance, Legal and the business, while coordinating closely with, and taking direction from, the regional Financial Crimes function.
Provide first-line advisory on KYC and customer due diligence – resolving incomplete-KYC and data-quality issues, escalating material matters, and supporting the timely onboarding of clients within standard industry timeframes.
Manage the increase in review volumes arising from data-driven periodic reviews across the full client population and the uplift to enhanced global KYC standards.
Review and disposition sanctions and negative-news screening alerts – clearing false positives and escalating genuine matches with supporting analysis to the relevant Financial Crimes and Legal stakeholders – and adapt to new screening tools and expanded matching logic that drive higher daily volumes.
Perform reviews of post-transaction daily screening, escalating sanctions-related alerts and ensuring same-day clearance to avoid delays to client applications and asset settlements.
Respond to time-sensitive trading-desk escalations relating to bond issuers and counterparties – conducting screenings and preparing risk assessments and escalation narratives for Financial Crimes and Legal stakeholders within tight deadlines.
Conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) reviews – completing due diligence forms, assessing screening results, and covering expanded scope such as beneficial-ownership, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis – obtaining the required approvals, escalating material findings to the regional Financial Crimes function, and presenting material cases to the relevant governance committee where required.
Coordinate with Operations and Sales teams, including outreach to distribution partners, to gather and analyze information for suspicious-transaction reviews prior to escalation.
Drive onshore delivery of the firm’s AML systems transformation and related regulatory-remediation initiatives – contributing to design, testing, tuning and rollout – while aligning to global standards and regional direction, and support the interim manual processes that remain in place pending implementation.
What You’ll Bring To The Role
8+ years of relevant experience in financial-crimes risk, AML/KYC and/or sanctions, ideally within asset or investment management, banking, or at a financial services regulator.
Hands-on experience across KYC and customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, sanctions and negative-news screening, alert dispositioning, and the escalation of genuine matches.
Solid, practical knowledge of sanctions regimes and sanctions screening is essential, including the assessment and escalation of potential matches and an understanding of the relevant regulatory expectations.
Working knowledge of the China regulatory environment (for example, People’s Bank of China and China Securities Regulatory Commission expectations), and an awareness of conflicts-of-law considerations between international sanctions requirements and the PRC Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law, is a strong advantage.
Familiarity with screening, transaction-monitoring and AML/KYC systems used in a financial services environment; experience supporting AML systems implementations or upgrades is a plus.
Based onshore in China (Shenzhen) with the right to work locally; full professional fluency in both English and Mandarin is required to operate effectively in this environment.
Strong understanding of AML/CFT and KYC requirements and first-line procedures; regulatory remediation and audit-response experience at a large, international firm is a plus.
Bachelor’s degree in business, finance or a related field; a recognized anti-money-laundering or financial-crimes certification is advantageous.
High integrity, sound judgment, and the ability to handle highly confidential information – including sensitive client data – with appropriate discretion.
What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley
At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. Company Overview

Morgan Stanley Investment Management China (MSIM China), strives to provide diverse investment management services to a full spectrum of clients across both individual and institutional investors. Established as a joint venture in 2008, MSIM China became fully owned by Morgan Stanley Investment Management in 2023.

Benefiting from the global perspective and risk management capability of Morgan Stanley, MSIM China has established a variety of mutual fund and private fund portfolios covering fixed income, active equity, quantitative equity, multi-asset and sustainable investing strategies. Our portfolios have won many prestigious awards, including Morningstar Awards and Golden Bull Awards, which is a testament to our expertise and capabilities.

Position Overview

The first-line Financial Crimes Risk team is embedded within the Investment Management business and serves as the first line of defense for financial-crimes risk. It is responsible for identifying, assessing, escalating and helping to remediate money-laundering, sanctions and reputational risks associated with the firm’s funds, managed accounts, distribution partners and clients. The team owns first-line know-your-customer (KYC), enhanced due diligence, screening and onboarding oversight, working within the firm’s global financial-crimes framework and in close partnership with the regional and global Financial Crimes functions, the business, Operations, Technology and Legal & Compliance. This role delivers dedicated onshore coverage for the Investment Management business in China while operating under the direction of the regional Financial Crimes function.

The Vice President, Financial Crimes Risk, is the dedicated onshore first-line financial-crimes resource for the firm’s Investment Management business in China, based in Shenzhen. Reporting to the local Chief Operating Office and matrixed into the regional Financial Crimes Risk team, the role provides advisory support and risk oversight across customer onboarding, screening, enhanced due diligence, transaction reviews and financial-crimes initiatives.

Working closely with Operations, Compliance, Legal and the business, and taking direction from the regional and global Financial Crimes functions, the role helps drive effective risk management, regulatory compliance and operational excellence as local anti-money-laundering (AML) and KYC requirements continue to expand – including full-population periodic reviews, enhanced screening, and multi-year AML systems transformation. A dedicated onshore presence is essential to engage local stakeholders in real time, meet local data-residency and privacy requirements, and ensure consistent, well-coordinated execution between the onshore business and the wider Financial Crimes organization.

What you'll do in the role: (1LOD)

Serve as the dedicated onshore first-line point of contact and financial-crimes subject-matter expert for the Investment Management business in China, providing real-time advisory and escalation support to Operations, Compliance, Legal and the business, while coordinating closely with, and taking direction from, the regional Financial Crimes function.

Provide first-line advisory on KYC and customer due diligence – resolving incomplete-KYC and data-quality issues, escalating material matters, and supporting the timely onboarding of clients within standard industry timeframes.

Manage the increase in review volumes arising from data-driven periodic reviews across the full client population and the uplift to enhanced global KYC standards.

Review and disposition sanctions and negative-news screening alerts – clearing false positives and escalating genuine matches with supporting analysis to the relevant Financial Crimes and Legal stakeholders – and adapt to new screening tools and expanded matching logic that drive higher daily volumes.

Perform reviews of post-transaction daily screening, escalating sanctions-related alerts and ensuring same-day clearance to avoid delays to client applications and asset settlements.

Respond to time-sensitive trading-desk escalations relating to bond issuers and counterparties – conducting screenings and preparing risk assessments and escalation narratives for Financial Crimes and Legal stakeholders within tight deadlines.

Conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) reviews – completing due diligence forms, assessing screening results, and covering expanded scope such as beneficial-ownership, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis – obtaining the required approvals, escalating material findings to the regional Financial Crimes function, and presenting material cases to the relevant governance committee where required.

Coordinate with Operations and Sales teams, including outreach to distribution partners, to gather and analyze information for suspicious-transaction reviews prior to escalation.

Drive onshore delivery of the firm’s AML systems transformation and related regulatory-remediation initiatives – contributing to design, testing, tuning and rollout – while aligning to global standards and regional direction, and support the interim manual processes that remain in place pending implementation.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

  • 8+ years of relevant experience in financial-crimes risk, AML/KYC and/or sanctions, ideally within asset or investment management, banking, or at a financial services regulator.
  • Hands-on experience across KYC and customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence, sanctions and negative-news screening, alert dispositioning, and the escalation of genuine matches.
  • Solid, practical knowledge of sanctions regimes and sanctions screening is essential, including the assessment and escalation of potential matches and an understanding of the relevant regulatory expectations.
  • Working knowledge of the China regulatory environment (for example, People’s Bank of China and China Securities Regulatory Commission expectations), and an awareness of conflicts-of-law considerations between international sanctions requirements and the PRC Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law, is a strong advantage.
  • Familiarity with screening, transaction-monitoring and AML/KYC systems used in a financial services environment; experience supporting AML systems implementations or upgrades is a plus.
  • Based onshore in China (Shenzhen) with the right to work locally; full professional fluency in both English and Mandarin is required to operate effectively in this environment.
  • Strong understanding of AML/CFT and KYC requirements and first-line procedures; regulatory remediation and audit-response experience at a large, international firm is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in business, finance or a related field; a recognized anti-money-laundering or financial-crimes certification is advantageous.
  • High integrity, sound judgment, and the ability to handle highly confidential information – including sensitive client data – with appropriate discretion.

We are seeking a 1st line Business Control Officer to serve as an embedded compliance professional mainly covering Fixed-income Department and Multi-assets Investment Department (“Departments”) in Beijing office of MSIM China. This role is a vital component of the First Line of Defense (1LOD), directly assisting the Department Head in owning and managing the compliance risks inherent in our investment activities, and covering other 1LOD issues, to manage compliance/risk issues from 1L perspectives. The successful candidate will act as the primary compliance liaison within the business, driving the integration of compliance into daily operations while maintaining a constructive and independent working relationship with the Compliance Department (2LOD).
What you’ll do in the role: (1LOD):
Compliance Monitoring & Surveillance:
Assist department heads to supervise and manage employees’ behaviors including but not limited to personal cell phone management, personal trading/OBI, E-comms CoC, information protection, insider trading prevention, outbound trips management, remote work and other applicable code of conduct.
Ensure that material incidents, breaches, or risks are promptly escalated to the 1st line BU risk and Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)/Compliance Department in strict accordance with laws and regulations/firm's policy.
Policy & Procedure Implementation:
Assist department heads to establish and implement annual P&P building/updating plan
Where there is new regulatory requirement or new business initiative, assist department head to set up new policies and procedures or revisit existing ones accordingly.
Drive and oversee the effective implementation of all firm-wide and company-wide policies and procedures within department. Identify and address gaps between policies and local business processes, developing or updating departmental working guidelines as necessary. Report on implementation status and challenges to department heads CCO/Compliance Department.
Compliance Training & Culture:
Coordinate team members to participate in Compliance training, conduct necessary self-review and testing, and report training/testing records to Compliance Department.
Assist/Coordinate Compliance Department to deliver necessary 1st line compliance training to team members (including FTCs/outsourcing workers/interns)
Timely track new regulatory requirements and other related information shared from Compliance. Deliver above information to team members/outsourcing workers/interns as appropriate.
Coordinate team members to complete periodic attestation as required by Compliance (such as annual COC commitment letter and other firm-required attestation).
Advisory & Review:
Provide timely, practical compliance advice to the department on day-to-day activities, leveraging a deep understanding of both regulations and business needs and making inquiry with Compliance as appropriate.
Review new products, investment instruments, initiatives, other business proposals and provide advice from 1st line perspective. If necessary, positively initiate discussion with Compliance and other internal control functions.
Assist department heads to manage and handle funds (including mutual funds and privately offered funds) periodical reports, mainly including four-eye review, coordination, development of standardized workflow.
Facilitation of Independent Reviews:
Upon request and within a reasonable scope, facilitate independent testing, inspections, and assessments conducted by the Compliance Department, internal audit or other independent review functions/parties. This includes providing controlled access to necessary documents and personnel for interviews, while the independent execution of the review remains with the review functions.
Assist department heads to execute remediation plans and report to review functions the stage result
Portfolio Surveillance team
Work as the backup for portfolio surveillance team, including coding the limits in the system, perform post-trade control etc.
Other BAU control work
What You'll Bring To The Role
Bachelor's or above degree in Law, Finance, Economics, or a related field. A relevant professional qualification (e.g., PRC BAR, CPA, CFA, FRM, or equivalent compliance certification) is preferred.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in compliance, internal audit, or risk management within a financial institution or experience from reputable accounting firm or law firm.
Strong ability to interpret regulations and translate them into actionable business requirements. Possess excellent judgment to balance business initiatives with regulatory constraints.
Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills, with the proven ability to influence and build trust with senior business personnel and to act as an effective bridge to the 2LOD.
Highly self-motivated, with the initiative to identify risks independently and the resilience to uphold standards within a demanding business environment.
Fluency in English is required.
Reporting Line
This role reports to Head of Business Control Unit. In accordance with local regulations, the professional performance is reviewed by CCO for specific compliance related activities.

We are seeking a 1st line Business Control Officer to serve as an embedded compliance professional mainly covering Fixed-income Department and Multi-assets Investment Department (“Departments”) in Beijing office of MSIM China. This role is a vital component of the First Line of Defense (1LOD), directly assisting the Department Head in owning and managing the compliance risks inherent in our investment activities, and covering other 1LOD issues, to manage compliance/risk issues from 1L perspectives. The successful candidate will act as the primary compliance liaison within the business, driving the integration of compliance into daily operations while maintaining a constructive and independent working relationship with the Compliance Department (2LOD).

What you’ll do in the role: (1LOD):

  • Compliance Monitoring & Surveillance:
  • Assist department heads to supervise and manage employees’ behaviors including but not limited to personal cell phone management, personal trading/OBI, E-comms CoC, information protection, insider trading prevention, outbound trips management, remote work and other applicable code of conduct.
  • Ensure that material incidents, breaches, or risks are promptly escalated to the 1st line BU risk and Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)/Compliance Department in strict accordance with laws and regulations/firm's policy.
  • Policy & Procedure Implementation:
  • Assist department heads to establish and implement annual P&P building/updating plan
  • Where there is new regulatory requirement or new business initiative, assist department head to set up new policies and procedures or revisit existing ones accordingly.
  • Drive and oversee the effective implementation of all firm-wide and company-wide policies and procedures within department. Identify and address gaps between policies and local business processes, developing or updating departmental working guidelines as necessary. Report on implementation status and challenges to department heads CCO/Compliance Department.
  • Compliance Training & Culture:
  • Coordinate team members to participate in Compliance training, conduct necessary self-review and testing, and report training/testing records to Compliance Department.
  • Assist/Coordinate Compliance Department to deliver necessary 1st line compliance training to team members (including FTCs/outsourcing workers/interns)
  • Timely track new regulatory requirements and other related information shared from Compliance. Deliver above information to team members/outsourcing workers/interns as appropriate.
  • Coordinate team members to complete periodic attestation as required by Compliance (such as annual COC commitment letter and other firm-required attestation).
  • Advisory & Review:
  • Provide timely, practical compliance advice to the department on day-to-day activities, leveraging a deep understanding of both regulations and business needs and making inquiry with Compliance as appropriate.
  • Review new products, investment instruments, initiatives, other business proposals and provide advice from 1st line perspective. If necessary, positively initiate discussion with Compliance and other internal control functions.
  • Assist department heads to manage and handle funds (including mutual funds and privately offered funds) periodical reports, mainly including four-eye review, coordination, development of standardized workflow.
  • Facilitation of Independent Reviews:
  • Upon request and within a reasonable scope, facilitate independent testing, inspections, and assessments conducted by the Compliance Department, internal audit or other independent review functions/parties. This includes providing controlled access to necessary documents and personnel for interviews, while the independent execution of the review remains with the review functions.
  • Assist department heads to execute remediation plans and report to review functions the stage result
  • Portfolio Surveillance team
  • Work as the backup for portfolio surveillance team, including coding the limits in the system, perform post-trade control etc.
  • Other BAU control work

What You'll Bring To The Role

  • Bachelor's or above degree in Law, Finance, Economics, or a related field. A relevant professional qualification (e.g., PRC BAR, CPA, CFA, FRM, or equivalent compliance certification) is preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in compliance, internal audit, or risk management within a financial institution or experience from reputable accounting firm or law firm.
  • Strong ability to interpret regulations and translate them into actionable business requirements. Possess excellent judgment to balance business initiatives with regulatory constraints.
  • Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills, with the proven ability to influence and build trust with senior business personnel and to act as an effective bridge to the 2LOD.
  • Highly self-motivated, with the initiative to identify risks independently and the resilience to uphold standards within a demanding business environment.

This role reports to Head of Business Control Unit. In accordance with local regulations, the professional performance is reviewed by CCO for specific compliance related activities.

In the Finance division, we act as a partner to business units around the globe by providing management, review, analysis and advisory services of the Firm’s financial and capital resources. This is a director level position within our Corporate Controllers, Reporting & Accounting Job Family which is responsible for the accuracy and control of the Firm’s books and records to produce the consolidated firm, segment and legal entities financial statements, including development, management and oversight of financial accounting & reporting systems as well as database management, including capital and liquidity reporting and external reporting functions.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

  • Collaborate with a varied group of colleagues in Finance and across the Firm
  • Responsible for and lead aspects of individual and team deliverables and projects, leveraging in-depth knowledge of Finance functional area, product and/or client segments
  • Adhere to the Firm's risk and regulatory standards, policies and controls; proactively identify ways to reduce risk in work
  • Act as a culture carrier; embody and set an example of the Firm's values and hold yourself and others accountable to Firm standards
  • Support legal entity accounting, ledger control and financial reporting processes
  • Support legal entity regulatory reporting processes
  • Support relevant internal control activities
  • Partner with finance colleagues and stakeholders to support various initiatives and projects.

  • In-depth knowledge of Finance functional area, product and/or client segment and technical skills, as well as of industry and competitive environment
  • Ability to operate independently with respect to most job responsibilities
  • Ability to provide positive and constructive feedback and innovate processes
  • Ability to identify and escalate risks
  • Ability and willingness to collaborate with different teams across various regions towards the achievement of common goals

jobs.descriptionText:
Company Overview
Morgan Stanley Securities (China) Co., Ltd. is Morgan Stanley’s securities business platform in China, and provides leading financial services to its clients in the People’s Republic of China and across the globe. Our businesses include underwriting and sponsoring of equities and bonds, securities principal trading, as well as other businesses approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC). jobs.title: Vice President Senior Global Operations Manager, China
jobs.descriptionText:
Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking is a leading global financial institution that provides advisory, investment banking, financing, corporate banking and capital markets services to corporations, financial institutions, financial sponsors and sovereign and supranational organizations worldwide.
Our teams of experts in close to 30 countries advise clients on their strategic development, helping them to grow and transform their businesses, and maximize their positive impact. Natixis CIB is committed to aligning its financing portfolio with a carbon neutrality path by 2050 while helping its clients reduce the environmental impact of their business.
As part of Groupe BPCE, the second largest banking group in France through the Banque Populaire and Caisse d’Epargne retail networks, Natixis CIB benefits from the Group’s financial strength and solid financial ratings (Standard & Poor's: A+, Moody's: A2, Fitch: A+, R&I: A+).
Job Description Summary
This role holds strategic responsibility for overseeing and optimizing Global Market and Treasury operations within the China market, ensuring operational excellence, robust risk management, and efficient transaction processing. The Senior Operations Manager will drive process improvements, lead automation initiatives, and contribute to departmental projects, setting the standard for operational efficiency and regulatory compliance. The impact of this role extends to strengthening the organization's operational capabilities and contributing to strategic business growth in China.
Main Responsibilities:
Operational Duties / Business-as-Usual (BAU)
Project Management & Contribution: Lead or significantly contribute to UAT (User Acceptance Testing) for new systems, technology implementations, and participate in or lead mini-projects aimed at streamlining operations or expanding capabilities.
Treasury Forecasting & Optimization: Oversee the treasury forecasting process, ensuring accuracy and proactively identifying opportunities for cash flow optimization and liquidity management.
Payment & SSI Strategy: Drive the strategic management of payment processes and SSI data integrity to minimize settlement risks and ensure efficient cash movements.
Trade Confirmation & Reconciliation Excellence: Establish and maintain best practices for trade confirmation drafting, matching, and all reconciliation activities with external agents, ensuring rapid and accurate break resolution.
Fee Management & Collateral Optimization: Oversee fee management processes and contribute to the strategic optimization of collateral management to support trading activities.
Issue Resolution & Escalation Management: Manage and resolve complex operational issues, establish escalation protocols, and ensure effective communication with all stakeholders.
Governance, Compliance and Risk Management
Risk Management & Control Enhancement: Continuously assess the operational risk landscape, develop and implement enhanced control frameworks, and ensure all activities are compliant with internal policies and external regulations.
Regulatory Reporting Leadership: Ensure the accurate, timely, and compliant execution of all local regulatory reporting requirements, acting as a key point of contact for regulatory inquiries.
Continuous Improvement & Innovation
Process Improvement & Automation Leadership: Proactively identify, propose, and lead the implementation of process improvements and automation initiatives to enhance efficiency, reduce operational risk, and control costs.
Improve efficiency of the team by doing regular sit in with minutes and adjusting the documents in place to tracks unitary time of every process and create synergies between her/his teams
Leadership & People Management (For Leader Roles only)
Strategic Oversight & Execution: Provide leadership and direction for all Global Markets and Treasury operational activities, ensuring adherence to global standards and local regulations with a focus on achieving zero defaults and zero delays.
Team Development & Mentorship: Mentor and guide junior team members, fostering a culture of continuous learning, operational excellence, and proactive problem-solving.
Maintain knowledge to a high level by reviewing the skill matrix and propose action plan to improve knowledge sharing.
Manage wisely holidays to avoid end of year packs.
Report and monitor the capacity management of the teams and raise early warning to her/his management
Required Skills:
Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field; relevant professional certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM) are a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in operations within global markets and treasury functions, with a significant portion in a leadership or management role.
Demonstrated experience in leading operational projects, process re-engineering, or automation initiatives within a financial services context.
Proven track record of managing operational risks and implementing robust control frameworks.
Skills and Competencies
Functional Skills (Role-Critical)
Deep expertise in a wide range of global markets products and complex transaction lifecycles.
Advanced understanding of treasury operations, cash management, and liquidity principles.
Proficiency in designing and implementing effective reconciliation strategies.
Comprehensive knowledge of payment systems and international payment flows.
Specific Skills
In-depth Knowledge of Chinese Financial Market Regulations: Expert understanding of current and evolving regulations governing foreign exchange, securities, derivatives, and interbank markets in China. Ability to interpret and apply these regulations to operational processes.
Language Proficiency: Fluent in Mandarin (spoken and written) is critical for navigating complex local business environments and regulatory interactions. Strong command of English is essential for global liaison.
Chinese Market Operational Expertise: Extensive experience and nuanced understanding of local market practices, participant behaviors, and operational nuances in the Chinese financial landscape.
Transformative Skills
Strategic Process Design & Automation: Proven ability to conceptualize, design, and lead the implementation of transformative process improvements and automation solutions using modern technologies.
Basic project Management knowledge: ability to plan, execute, and monitor some small projects (scoping, timelines, and resources, including leading UAT efforts).
Analytical & Critical Thinking: ability to analyze complex operational challenges, identify root causes, and develop innovative, data-driven solutions.
Stakeholder Management: Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills to effectively manage relationships with internal business units, external counterparties, and technology providers.
Change Management: Ability to effectively drive and manage change within the team and across the organization, ensuring smooth transitions.

jobs.descriptionText:
Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Development Lead to join our technology team and play a key role in designing, developing, and maintaining robust, scalable trading control systems that power Standard Chartered's digital banking platform. The successful candidate will lead technical initiatives, build platform 0-1, and contribute to architectural decisions that with major business impact to our global financial market business.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Architecture
Design and develop high-performance, scalable backend services and APIs using modern technologies
Implement microservices architecture patterns and distributed system design principles
Ensure system reliability, performance, and security across all backend services
Drive adoption of best practices in code quality, testing, and deployment
Make architectural decisions and contribute to technical strategy and roadmap planning
Development & Implementation
Build robust RESTful APIs and microservices using Java, Spring Boot, and related technologies
Implement secure, efficient database designs and optimize query performance
Develop event-driven architectures using messaging systems (Solace, Kafka)
Integrate with third-party systems and external APIs following banking industry standards
Implement comprehensive monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions
Collaboration & Communication
Work closely with DEV, SRE, QA, BA, product managers, and business stakeholders
Conduct thorough code reviews and provide constructive feedback
Lead technical discussions and facilitate knowledge sharing sessions
Participate in technical interviews and contribute to team building initiatives
Quality & Compliance
Ensure all backend systems comply with banking regulations and security standards
Implement comprehensive testing strategies including unit, integration, and performance testing
Drive continuous improvement in development processes and methodologies
Maintain high standards of documentation for systems and processes
Support production systems and participate in on-call rotations when required
Skills And Experience
Must-have Skills
Application Design, Architecture
Software Development
Leadership
Other Skills
AI
Qualifications
Key Experiences
8+ years of experience in development with strong Java expertise, with at least 5+ years in a leadership role.
Proficiency in Spring Framework (Spring Boot)
Extensive experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL databases (Redis)
Extensive experience with messaging systems (Solace, Apache Kafka)
Strong understanding of microservices architecture and distributed systems
Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)
Experience in CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices
Experience with API design and development (REST, GraphQL)
Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
Ability to mentor and lead a team of engineers, fostering an environment of innovation and continuous learning.
Certifications / Qualifications
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
Languages
English
About Standard Chartered
We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.
Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.
Together We
Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term
What We Offer
In line with our Fair Pay Charter,
we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.
Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Job Summary
Providing direct advisory services to customers on portfolio construction and portfolio review;
Ensuring SCB offers a differentiated, best-in-class, consistent advisory proposition across customer segments.
This will primarily involve providing professional expert advice to customers using the SCB advisory process for asset allocation, portfolio construction and portfolio review based on the full understanding of the customer's financial position, objectives, risk tolerance and other circumstances (but not including tax status).
The Investment Advisor also acts as a subject matter expert to customers/frontline staff on holistic view of the market, and support SCB wealth strategy in providing to higher value customers a higher level of customer service, and growing recurring income faster than the transaction-based income
Key Responsibilities
Portfolio/Investment Construction and Review for Assigned Customers
Partner with 8-12 relationship managers RMs and act as an investment advisor to assigned customers of those RMs. For IAs Priority Banking, we would seek to provide this portfolio review service to at least the top 25% of Priority customers - as a guideline customer with combined Deposits+WM AUM of $200k & above.]
Grow AUM of customers through investment advisory services, by proposing customer-specific portfolio solutions that will drive net growth in customer portfolios.
Understand, acknowledge and comply with the requirements on individual accountabilities and responsibilities of the job set out in applicable local laws and regulations as well as SCB internal policies
Effectively ensure and intensify internal controls by keeping abreast with developments of applicable local laws and regulations on accountabilities
Perform job duties with diligence, contribute to efforts as an individual or as a team member so as to avoid any actual or potential legal sanctions, regulatory penalties, material financial loss, or adverse reputational impact on the Bank
Be responsible for failure to follow relevant rules and processes, failure to properly perform the responsibilities, and implement corrections
Cooperate with any investigations or reviews on regulatory failure such as accountability review
Fully comply with all the regulatory requirements related to Consumer Rights Protection, uphold the robust mindset of Consumer Rights Protection, complete the Consumer Rights Protection themed training and workshop in due course, prevent the potential infringements of consumer rights, participate the public education, EV or other activities to uplift the public awareness about Consumer Rights Protection
Strategy
Based on materials issued by Group and Country Investment Advisory and Strategy teams, provide market briefings for RMs/branches/Hubs
Based on materials issued by Group and Country Wealth Solutions teams, provide updates on investment advisory process changes to RMs
Business
Portfolio/Investment Diagnostics to Assigned RMs
Conduct one-on-one diagnostic reviews with each assigned RM on his/her portfolio at least once a month, to:
Align customer portfolios with their investment objectives, and aligning portfolios with house views
Balance asset allocation and thematic plays
Processes
Provide investment consultation in the customers’ best interests using the SCB advisory process, rather than focussing on the sale of specific products.
Help the customer to achieve his or her objectives, in the context of the customer's current needs/circumstances, in compliance with all regulatory and bank requirements and with the highest professional standards.
People & Talent
Outstanding ability to provide leadership, guidance and inspiration to the customers, RMs and other partners
Strong sense of self-motivation and discipline in execution
Excellent communication and negotiation skills with the ability to influence outcomes
Ability to network with internal and external business stakeholders.
Risk Management
Understand, acknowledge and comply with the requirements on individual accountabilities and responsibilities of the job set out in applicable local laws and regulations as well as SCB internal policies
Governance
Perform job duties with diligence, contribute to efforts as an individual or as a team member so as to avoid any actual or potential legal sanctions, regulatory penalties, material financial loss, or adverse reputational impact on the Bank
Regulatory & Business Conduct
Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

WRB Affluent team

Key Responsibilities

Integrated seamlessly with multiple endpoints, incorporating compliance checks, position management, locates, order marking, limits, frontrunning prevention, and command/control. Full Time
Job Reference #
341856BR
City
Shanghai
Key Responsibilities
Price structured and mildly bespoke exotics with FX, Rates, Credit or Equity underlyings
Perform iterations on trade attributes and market data for analysis
Liaise with on-shore pricing teams and trading
Develop and maintain existing pricing tools
Help on daily pricing flow, term sheet, marketing material, ad-hoc analysis
Help upgrade and maintain automated pricing tool in Python
Add new products, features and unit tests
Run regular reports
Develop and maintain automated termsheet generation tool in excel vba.
Keep track of the daily flows for market & client profiling, help on market color report
Trade idea generation based on current market environment.
AI development to facilitate process and generate innovation.
The team
The Shanghai Fixed Income Structuring & Pricing team is a core part of UBS Global Markets Structuring in APAC. The team supports the origination, pricing, execution and lifecycle management of a broad range of structured products across Rates, FX, Credit and Hybrid asset classes. The team works closely with Sales, Trading, Structuring, Quantitative Analytics and Technology functions across the region.
The team is responsible for daily pricing and execution support for structured note and OTC transactions, product analysis, termsheet preparation, automation initiatives and strategic infrastructure enhancements. We actively drive innovation through digitalization and AI-enabled solutions, aiming to improve operational efficiency, scalability and client responsiveness.
Working in a fast-paced and collaborative environment, team members gain exposure to a wide spectrum of structured products, interact with stakeholders across APAC and contribute to the development of next-generation structuring and pricing capabilities.

jobs.title: APAC Algo Trading Low Latency C++ Developer
jobs.descriptionText:
Job Type
Full Time
Job Reference #
327174BR
City
Shanghai
Key Responsibilities
Join a high-performance team building ultra-low latency trading systems where nanoseconds matter. You’ll design and implement a trading rules engine for real-time controls using a hybrid of FPGA hardware and high-performance C++, enabling deterministic execution and rapid interaction with the markets.
Design and implement real-time trading rules and risk checks using FPGA (Verilog/VHDL) or C++.
Architect cycle-accurate FPGA designs and high-speed network interfaces (10/25/40/100GbE, RoCEv2) is preferred.
Build simulation and verification frameworks for FPGA reliability.
Drive full FPGA design flow (synthesis, place & route, timing closure).
Interface C++ applications with FPGA hardware for real-time orchestration.
Implement lock-free data structures and concurrency control in Linux.
Build low-latency network apps using kernel bypass (e.g., Rivermax).
Analyze system performance and resolve latency bottlenecks.
Collaborate with global IT, Quants, and Traders across asset classes.
Provide Level 3 support for production systems.
The team
You’ll be part of the Algorithmic Trading Team based out of Shanghai within the Execution Services, delivering latency-sensitive infrastructure for Algorithmic Execution, Smart Order Routing, Internalization, and Real-time Controls across global markets.
Your Skills And Experience
7+ years in FPGA (Verilog/VHDL) or low-latency C++ development.
Expert in C++17/20/23, Linux system programming, concurrency.
Deep knowledge of FPGA toolchains (Vivado, Quartus), timing closure.
Experience with high-speed networking and hardware acceleration.
Strong background in shared memory IPC and lock-free systems.
Familiarity with market microstructure and trading protocols (FIX, ITCH) is a plus.
Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field.
Performance-obsessed and precision-driven.
A hands-on engineer who thrives in fast-paced environments.
A collaborative communicator.
Self-motivated with a passion for solving complex technical challenges.

jobs.descriptionText:
Job Type
Full Time
Job Reference #
338539BR
City
Shanghai
Key Responsibilities
Are you organized and independent in driving a complex business forward? Do you thrive in a team environment, blending strategic planning with operational execution to ensure business targets are met in a risk conscious and compliant manner? If so, this role might be perfect for you since it provides a unique opportunity for someone passionate about making a significant impact and contributing to our ongoing success.
We are looking for a highly driven, analytical, forward-thinking individual to join our APAC COO team in Shanghai, China, to support and help maintain a robust and well-controlled operating environment for Unified Global Markets (UGM), Global Markets Distribution APAC.
In this role, you will be responsible for:
Performing periodic controls under the pre-defined control plans for UGM Business;
Investigate and escalation of finding(s) being observed from the control review;
Prepare control summary for escalation to UGM Management and relevant governance forum(s);
Identify potential opportunities to automate and simplify the existing control plans to improve efficiency and aligning risk control frameworks globally
The team
The UGM Global Markets COO Distribution APAC team is a highly strategic team that is responsible for the formulation, implementation and support initiatives, overseeing business operation and processes and controls that impact our client’s experience. You will have broad exposure across UGM Global Markets in other regions in APAC and globally as well as Global Wealth Management.
As part of the team, you will have a pivotal role in supporting the implementation of strategic plans & changes across all product segments. This includes Equity, Foreign Exchange, Fixed Income, Structured Products, Direct Access Clients, and Sales Distribution. Each of these product segments presents unique opportunities and challenges, which the COO team contributions will be instrumental in helping us meet our business targets and ambitions, alongside managing our daily business operations in the APAC region.
Your Skills And Experience
Relevant experience in Global markets or Front Office support functions within a financial institution;
Analytical and capable of presenting and interpreting information to support decision making;
Liaising and coordinating key stakeholders across various divisions and functions;
Manage multiple priorities, and ensure completion of deliverables in a timely fashion;
